problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(4,-1),(17,-3),$ and $(10,-1).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(3,2)$
- $(-1,1)$
- $(5,1)$
worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-1-0}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 17 & 10 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(-1,1),(2,3),(5,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
